summary.headline: GACL Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR1,358 crore (from INR1,083 crore) and PAT to ~INR79 crore (from INR16 crore), with EBITDA margin on total income at 15.74%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue from operations was about INR1,358 crore versus INR1,083 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR222 crore (from INR133 crore) and PAT of about INR79 crore (from INR16 crore). H1 FY27 revenue was INR2,602 crore and EBITDA INR451 crore, with management citing better realisations in chlorotoluene, phosphoric acid, hydrogen peroxide and caustic soda. Operations were affected by plant shutdowns, grid disturbances and feedstock constraints, and average plant utilisation was about 92%. Management also reported higher renewable power share (55% in Q2), lower H1 power tariff (INR7.09/unit vs INR7.6), and sharper JV (GNAL) performance.

segments.name: Chlorotoluene
segments.commentary: Plant utilisation ramped to about 90%; pricing up almost 100% YoY in the quarter. Phase 1 downstream units targeted by March 2027.

segments.name: Caustic soda group
segments.commentary: Pricing up about 10% additional in the quarter; liquid exports about 5 KT/month (~60,000 t/yr) and solid exports 10,000-12,000 t/month. Dahej 200 TPD flaking facility targeted December 2026.

segments.name: Phosphoric acid
segments.commentary: Pricing up about 44% in the quarter; export footprint expanded. Food-grade phosphoric acid expansion under implementation.

segments.name: Hydrogen peroxide
segments.commentary: Pricing up 31% over previous quarter. Electronic-grade H2O2 plant targeted around January 2028.

segments.name: GACL-NALCO Alkalies & Chemicals (GNAL JV)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up ~14% (management also cited ~23% in Q&A) and EBITDA up ~19%; H1 sales up 27%, EBITDA up 73%, PBT moved from loss of INR36 crore to profit of INR8 crore.

segments.name: Hydrazine hydrate
segments.commentary: GACL is India's sole producer; ramp-up is slow and management declined to give yield or utilisation data, preferring a longer evaluation horizon.

guidance_outlook: Renewable share targeted at 60% by March 2027 (from 49% cited in Q&A), with power cost expected to fall to about INR6.18/kWh; long-term target 80% RE and power cost below INR6 by FY30.
Aspiration of INR10,000 crore+ revenue and EBITDA margin above 20% by FY31 under Project Ahvaan; management called it a medium-term aspiration, not guidance.
Chlorine integration targeted to rise from about 45% to about 75% in two to three years as HCl and other chlorine-consuming capex commissions.
Management said current market realisations are better than Q2, particularly for caustic soda, but declined to quantify, citing energy cost impacts.
Funding for future expansion to be a mix of internal accruals and borrowings; no specific capex or year-end debt figure given.
capex_capacity: 200 TPD caustic soda flaking facility at Dahej and cell element replacement targeted December 2026.
120 TPD HCl synthesis unit targeted around January 2027; a second HCl unit has in-principle Board approval, expected next year or later.
Chlorotoluene downstream Phase 1 units by March 2027; electronic-grade hydrogen peroxide around January 2028.
FY29: boilers, KOH expansion at Vadodara and second food-grade phosphoric acid plant at Dahej.
Closing capital WIP about INR434 crore; PP&E purchases of INR118 crore in H1; INR32.33 crore equity invested in CleanMax SPV for 62.7 MW renewable projects.
demand_pricing: Domestic sales up 29% YoY in Q2; exports up 14%. Export expansion for phosphoric acid, caustic soda prills, methylene dichloride; chlorotoluene sales in US, UK and Europe; benzaldehyde exports to US commenced.

Chlorine realisation improved from substantially negative levels during the quarter as industry downstream consumption rose; merchant chlorine pipeline about 150 TPD, outside sales about 700-750 t/day.
Management sees opportunity in European caustic exports as European capacity phases out; India positioned to become world number 3 producer.
Management said R132 refrigerant capacity additions should lift methylene chloride demand within chloromethanes, as R22 phases out.
Management is pursuing long-term commercial arrangements in selected product categories.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation levels for H1, Q1 vs Q2 split and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall utilisation averaged about 92%; chlorotoluene plant ramped to about 90%. Other plants were marginally lower YoY due to grid disturbances and shutdowns. No Q1/Q2 split given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel cost rise from INR370 crore to INR421 crore sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a DISCOM rate rise of about INR0.45/unit and a delay in ABRen long-term RE commissioning, partly offset by short-term RE. H1 power cost is INR0.57/unit lower YoY, with a slight overrun vs budget.

qa_highlights.question: Power mix and cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 mix: DISCOM plus GNAL captive 43% (81 MW), short-term RE 28% (52 MW), owned wind 29% (53 MW). Full-year power cost projected at INR6.95/kWh; target 60% RE by March 2027 with cost falling to about INR6.18/kWh.

qa_highlights.question: Chlorine integration and sales of chlorine to outside customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration about 45%, pipeline sales about 150 TPD, outside sales about 700-750 t/day. Target 75% integration in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Most profitable products and EBITDA contribution of value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorotoluene pricing up almost 100% YoY, phosphoric acid up about 44%, hydrogen peroxide up 31%, caustic group up about 10%. Management declined to split H1 EBITDA by product.

qa_highlights.question: Capex funding, EBITDA per tonne at 75% integration, and year-end debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give EBITDA per tonne or capex quantum. Funding to be mix of internal accruals and borrowings; year-end capex and borrowing not guided. Kearney is preparing the growth strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Post-quarter realisations and new large caustic capacities?
qa_highlights.answer: Current realisations are relatively better than Q2, especially caustic soda, but energy cost impacts remain and no number given. Management's response to new capacity is cost leadership and global market focus.

risks_watch: Grid disturbances, plant shutdowns and feedstock constraints weighed on non-chlorotoluene plant utilisation; reliability needs to improve.
Large new caustic soda capacities from private players could pressure realisations; chlorine pricing remains volatile.
Power cost sensitivity: 43% of H1 power still from grid and captive sources; DISCOM tariff rises and low wind periods hit margins.
Hydrazine hydrate ramp-up timing and yields undisclosed.
Rising capex with cash flow concerns; funding mix and year-end debt not guided, and a new JV investment of INR32.33 crore was made.
Sharp rise in other financial liabilities (INR74 crore to INR251 crore, attributed to dividend payable and capex creditors) and other current liabilities (INR70 crore to INR105 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the year-on-year turnaround, realisations and renewable energy progress, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers: management declined to quantify capex, funding, EBITDA per tonne, year-end debt and product-wise EBITDA, citing market cyclicality.
key_quotes: Importantly, our external sales revenue of INR1,334.79 crores in Q2 and INR2,559.63 crores in H1 present our highest quarterly and half-yearly sales in the last two decades.

This remains a medium-term aspiration rather than near-term financial guidance, and its achievement will naturally depend on market conditions, project execution, energy and raw material prices, and the chemical cycle.
The chlorine prices has been substantially negative, which has improved significantly during the quarter to maintain the ECU levels.

oneOffs.what: Chlorotoluene pricing up almost 100% YoY and phosphoric acid up about 44% in the quarter, a sharp price-led step-up rather than a recurring base; management did not split EBITDA by product
Q2 FY26 PAT of about INR16 crore on PBT of INR13 crore is a very weak year-ago base, so the YoY jump in PAT (~INR79 crore) is inflated by base effects

quality.why: Revenue rose about 25% (INR1,083 crore to INR1,358 crore) mainly on price realisations in chlorotoluene, phosphoric acid, hydrogen peroxide and caustic soda, with domestic sales up 29% and exports up 14% adding some volume; the brief does not state a volume growth figure, and the sharp PAT jump is partly flattered by a very weak year-ago base, while price spikes that may not persist are not one-of
